Alex — great to chat this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call recap:
- Primary use case: in-product conversational assistant (support + guided workflows).
- Current expected volume: ballpark 50M–200M tokens/month; you mentioned an initial expected run-rate ~120M/month with aggressive growth.
- Latency targets: 95th p95 goal ~= 250ms for interactive flows; critical flows need better 99th p99 awareness.
- Target unit economics: you indicated aiming for roughly $100–$150 per 1M tokens (ideally closer to $125/1M).
- Budget: roughly $15k–$30k/month target for model inference spend in the near term.

Key cost/latency levers we discussed:
- Hosting tier: Hosted Standard (cost-optimized) vs Hosted Low-latency / Premium (faster kernels, reserved capacity) vs Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) — tradeoffs explained below.
- Batching & prefix/KV caching: can reduce per-token cost substantially for repeat contexts; depends on your request distribution and session stickiness.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming reduces perceived latency for users but slightly increases compute overhead in some model runtimes.
- SLO-driven pricing: if you need a hard 100–200ms SLO we recommend reserved capacity (dedicated) or a low-latency hosted tier — price delta is typically material vs cost-optimized paths.

Attachments: I attached our pricing options PDF and the MAU/token estimate template we walked through (redwood-pricing-options.pdf, mau_estimates.xlsx).

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm expected steady-state monthly tokens and peak QPS/SLO (reply with numbers below).
2) Run a short eval: we can provision a trial with 10M evaluation tokens and run a 24–72h benchmark against a sample prompt set you provide. Rafael (cc'd) will scope the benchmark.
3) Tech deep-dive: 30–45m demo of batching/streaming and dedicated sizing (suggest Tue 10am PT / Wed 1pm ET) — confirm availability.
4) Procurement: once we align on target unit economics and model choice, we’ll provide an indicative pricing band and a mutual action plan for PO/contract.

Subject: Re: RE: Cost & latency trade-offs — post-call recap and next steps

Alex — thanks for the numbers, that helps a lot. Rafael (solutions eng) and Neha (sales eng) are looped to scope the benchmark and pick the best serving path. High-level ballpark bands (very indicative) below to help procurement start planning — we’ll follow with a tailored quote after the benchmark and an expected commit level: 

Indicative unit-cost bands (per 1M tokens, USD) — ballpark, pre-discount:
- Hosted Standard (cost-optimized): $120–$160 / 1M tokens — good for non-strict SLOs and bursty traffic; uses dynamic pooling and higher batching.
- Hosted Low-latency (premium): $240–$360 / 1M tokens — optimized kernels, lower queuing, better tail latency.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity, monthly commit): $80–$140 / 1M tokens (depends on instance sizing, quantization, and commit). With a 12mo commit and quantized runtime we can approach the low end.

Notes on levers and expected impact:
- Batching & prefix/KV caching: for your assistant with repeatable contexts we typically see 20–50% reduction in token cost on workloads with good cache hit rates. The exact number depends on session stickiness and request lengths.
- Streaming: perceived latency improves (users see first tokens sooner) — overhead depends on model and runtime but expect a modest 5–15% increase in compute cost vs non-streaming for the same prompt in many cases. In practice we often recommend streaming for UX-sensitive flows while using batching/caching for background/async calls.
- SLO-driven pricing: if you need guaranteed p95 <200ms, we recommend reserved capacity (dedicated) or the low-latency hosted tier. Pricing delta versus Hosted Standard can be ~1.5–2.5x depending on desired tail guarantees.

Proposed quick actions: 
1) Rafael can run a 24–72h benchmark on your representative prompt set. We’ll provision a trial environment (10M eval tokens) and return: observed p50/p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens in that run (with and without streaming), and recommendations for tier/commit.
2) If numbers look good, we’ll produce an indicative pricing sheet tied to commit levels (30/60/90 day cadence).

I’ll attach the benchmark checklist and a short note on how we measure caching hit rates. Rafael — can you confirm availability to run the trial starting Tue after the tech deep-dive?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
